statement.text:
Consider the group

          M = ⟨x, y, z, t | [x, y] = [y, z] = [z, x] = (x, t) = (y, t) = (z, t) = 1⟩
where [x, y] = x−1 y −1 xy and (x, t) = x−1 t−1 x−1 txt. The subgroup H = ⟨x, t, y⟩ is
isomorphic to the braid group B4 , and is normally complemented by N = (zx−1 )M .
Is N a free group (?) of countably infinite rank (?) on which H acts faithfully by
conjugation?                                                           D. L. Johnson
  ∗ As pointed by Y. Antolı́n, the group M is the Artin group of type D ; it is proved
in (B. Perron, J. P. Vannier, Math. Ann., 306, no. 2 (1996), 231–246) that N is a free
group of rank 3 and H acts on N faithfully by conjugation.
